title: 00 — Open Lakehouse: Index
html:
00 — Open Lakehouse: Index

The one idea: a modern data platform separates three things that used to be one product: open files (Parquet), an open table format on top of them (Iceberg or Delta), and a catalog that governs both. Engines come and go. This set explains each layer, how the pieces fit, and what changed in 2025 and 2026.

1. What this set is

The Data Engineering set explains the field: Spark, Delta Lake, the Databricks basics, streaming and orchestration. This set goes one level deeper, into the technologies a financial data platform is built from today:

  • How Apache Iceberg works inside: metadata, snapshots, commits, deletes, catalogs.
  • The columnar stack: Parquet and Arrow.
  • The Databricks services that run the lakehouse: Unity Catalog, Lakeflow, Databricks SQL, sharing, the AI stack, Lakebase and Apps.
  • The engines that run on a laptop: Polars, DuckDB, Daft, PyIceberg.
  • Retrieval and graphs, contracts and lineage, and a full A to Z of data terminology.

Every chapter follows the same plan: what it is, why it matters, the main ideas, code (run, with real output, or clearly marked "not run"), common mistakes, an exercise, questions to test yourself, and dated sources. Product status changes often, so every status claim says when it was checked (2026-10-26) and whether the sources agreed.

2. Chapter map

# Chapter What you get from it
01 Iceberg Table Anatomy Metadata tree, snapshots, manifests, the atomic commit, pruning, time travel
02 Iceberg Deletes, v3 and Maintenance Copy-on-write vs merge-on-read, deletion vectors, row lineage, variant, branches, maintenance, v4 proposals
03 Iceberg Catalogs and Interoperability REST catalog protocol, Polaris, Unity Catalog, Delta and UniForm, which engine reads what
04 Parquet, Arrow and the Columnar Stack Row groups, encodings, statistics, variant shredding, Arrow, ADBC, Flight SQL
05 Unity Catalog in Depth Securables, table types, volumes, privileges, ABAC, lineage, system tables
06 Lakeflow: Connect, Pipelines and Jobs Managed ingestion, declarative pipelines, AUTO CDC and SCD2, triggers, bundles
07 Databricks SQL, Compute and Performance Serverless, Photon, warehouses, predictive optimization, federation, metric views
08 Sharing and Collaboration Delta Sharing, Iceberg clients, Marketplace, Clean Rooms
09 The Databricks AI Stack MLflow 3, Model Serving, AI Functions, AI Search, hybrid retrieval, agents and MCP
10 Lakebase and Databricks Apps Operational Postgres next to the lakehouse, branching, synced tables, internal apps
11 Single-Node Engines Polars, DuckDB, DuckLake, Daft and PyIceberg, and when each fits
12 Graphs and Knowledge Graphs Property graphs vs RDF, GraphFrames, NetworkX, entity clusters, dated relationships
13 Contracts, Lineage and Observability ODCS v3.1, OpenLineage, column lineage, data quality monitoring
14 Data Terminology A to Z Every data term used in this set and the companion sets, in plain words
15 What's New in the Lakehouse, 2026 A dated list of the changes that matter, with sources
16 Statistics for Data Quality and Drift PSI, KS, robust z-scores, seasonal baselines, and what a drift breach should do
17 Personal Data and India's DPDP Act The 2025 Rules' phased dates, and what they mean for landing, extraction and outside models
18 Securing Agents and MCP Tools OWASP LLM and agentic risks, tool pinning, untrusted content, least agency
19 Staying Current: News Sources and Feeds The release-note, GitHub and regulator feeds behind the site's news page, and how to add one

3. Reading order

  1. Formats first: 04 → 01 → 02 → 03. You can't reason about a table format until you know what a Parquet file holds.
  2. The platform: 05 → 06 → 07 → 08.
  3. AI and applications: 09 → 10 → 12.
  4. The laptop path: 11, then 13.
  5. Quality, privacy and safety: 16, 17, 18.
  6. Keep open the whole time: 14 (terminology), 15 (what's new) and 19 (where the news comes from).

If you are coming from the Financial Data Engine course, read 01, 02, 06 and 13 first: they go deeper on the storage, pipeline and contract ideas the course uses.
